summary:
**AstroGuard – Astronaut Health System**

AstroGuard is a web-based astronaut health and mission management platform designed to support astronauts during space missions by bringing essential health information, personal mission data, and daily activities together in one place.

The platform provides an Astronaut Portal where users can access astronaut profiles, monitor health-related information, review daily health and mission details, and stay informed about their scheduled activities. It also incorporates destination information to help astronauts explore and understand the celestial bodies associated with their missions.

By centralizing important information into an accessible dashboard, AstroGuard aims to simplify access to mission-related data, support health awareness, and improve the organization of astronauts' daily routines.

Developed using React, Django REST Framework, and Supabase, the project demonstrates how modern web technologies can be combined to create an integrated astronaut health and mission information system.
details:
AstroGuard – Astronaut Health System

1. Project Overview

AstroGuard is a web-based astronaut health and mission information management system designed to centralize essential astronaut information and support health awareness during space missions.

Space missions require astronauts to manage multiple aspects of their daily routines while remaining informed about their health, activities, and mission objectives. AstroGuard addresses this challenge by bringing relevant information together through a centralized and accessible platform.

2. What Does AstroGuard Do?

AstroGuard provides an Astronaut Portal that allows users to access and explore information related to their space missions.

The platform focuses on the following areas:

  • Astronaut Information: Provides an overview of astronaut profiles and relevant personal and mission information.
  • Health Monitoring: Organizes health-related information to help astronauts stay informed about their health status.
  • Daily Mission Information: Presents daily activities, schedules, and important information that astronauts need throughout their missions.
  • Destination Information: Provides information about the celestial destination associated with a mission, helping users better understand the environment they are exploring.
  • Centralized Dashboard: Brings essential astronaut and mission information together in one interface, making it easier to access and navigate.

3. How Does It Work?

AstroGuard follows a client-server architecture.

The frontend, developed with React and Vite, provides the user interface through which astronauts can navigate the platform and access information.

The backend, developed using Django REST Framework, handles application logic and exposes REST API endpoints that allow the frontend to communicate with the system.

Supabase provides the PostgreSQL database infrastructure for storing and managing application data.

Through this architecture, the different components work together to provide an organized experience for accessing astronaut profiles, health information, daily activities, and mission destinations.

4. Benefits and Potential Impact

AstroGuard aims to make astronaut-related information more accessible and organized by bringing different categories of information into a unified platform.

Its potential benefits include:

  • Improving accessibility to astronaut and mission information.
  • Simplifying the organization of daily mission activities.
  • Supporting awareness of astronaut health-related information.
  • Providing convenient access to destination information.
  • Demonstrating how integrated digital platforms can support future space exploration activities.

5. Our Objectives

Our main objective is to explore how modern web technologies can contribute to astronaut health awareness and mission information management.

We aim to develop a foundation that can evolve into a more comprehensive astronaut support platform, with potential future improvements such as expanded health analytics, real-time monitoring, automated alerts, and deeper integration with space agency data.

6. Technologies Used

The project was developed using:

  • React: Frontend user interface.
  • Vite: Frontend development and production build tooling.
  • Django: Backend application framework.
  • Django REST Framework: REST API development and communication.
  • Supabase: PostgreSQL database infrastructure.
  • Git and GitHub: Version control and collaborative development.

7. Future Possibilities

AstroGuard provides a starting point for a broader astronaut support ecosystem. Future development could introduce real-time health data integration, personalized health insights, automated notifications, enhanced mission planning, and additional space environment information.

Our vision is to make essential astronaut health and mission information more accessible through a unified digital platform that can support the evolving needs of human space exploration.
